Extreme weather

Hurricane Season

A storm can take several power plants out of service at once. Build a Puerto Rico grid with enough room to recover.

Play Hurricane Season↗ See what’s at stake ↓

Free to play in your browser. Choose your difficulty in the game.

Location
San Juan, Puerto Rico
Starts in
2000
Time to plan
20 years

The situation

Your starting point

You start in 2000 with oil, gas and coal plants serving an island grid. There are years to build before the scenario's major hurricane, but the utility still has to operate and pay its bills in the meantime.

Storm damage can affect several plants together. The spare capacity that covers an ordinary outage may be too little for an emergency that also puts pressure on fuel costs.

The choices

What will you do?

  1. 01

    Build before repairs are needed

    Decide how much preparation you can afford while the grid is operating normally. New construction takes time that an emergency will not give back.

  2. 02

    Consider what can fail together

    Look beyond the loss of one plant. Compare a larger reserve with a fleet whose sources do not all share the same weaknesses.

  3. 03

    Fund the recovery

    Keep cash available for the period of reduced output and expensive fuel. Restoring supply and staying solvent are part of the same job.

Put your plan to the test

What would a utility built with hurricane recovery in mind do differently?

Build, watch what happens, and try a different approach. The grid is yours to run.
